newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - Aug 15.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - Aug 15.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:
(2x4 Std&Btr) WEEKLY MIDWEEK PREV WK YR AGO

COMMENT - Last week's rally in Western and Canadian items ran out of steam and producers rode their order files to hold prices firm, Random Lengths said in its end-week review. But producers were wary of the accelerating retreat in Southern Pine prices, the lumber reporting agency said.
Some Southern Pine producers openly admitted that they would be forced to lower prices by next week if sales don't pick up, but others claimed order files stretching into September.

Most prices finished unchanged to slightly higher with the exception of Southern Pine, where cuts of $15-25 pulled down the overall Framing Composite Index by $5. In one of the flattest downward trends on record, the Composite has fallen just over $2 per week through a seven-week period, Random Lengths said.
Trading remained heavy in mixed loads and quick shipments as dealers avoided forward purchases. This kept reloads and distributors busy shipping truckloads out of their inventories.

But they were in no hurry to replace, the agency said. Wholesalers focused on selling what they owned and reported fair success filling holes in customers' stocks. But the narrow spread between mill quotes and retailer ideas of prices kept margins thin. A hoped-for round of buying by treaters and home centers ahead of the long Labor Day weekend did not develop and both groups continued to buy sparingly, Random Lengths said.

Western mills continued a drumbeat of complaints about poor rail service and the railroads' seeming inability to restore an even flow of shipments. Boards bounced back after several weeks of weakening prices when buyers decided to replenish, it said.

The Ponderosa shop market was also upbeat, leading to predictions by some traders that prices would stabilize in September. Radius edge decking, the lone bright spot for Southern producers, cooled off, Random Lengths said.
Canadian fee-free quota shipments as of August 6 were at 39.6 percent of the July/Sept quarterly quota and 38.3 pct of the annual April/March quota, the agency said.
